chapters.title: Solomon Asks for Wisdom
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 1

At Gibeon

1Solomon son of David established himself firmly over his kingdom, and the LORD his God was with him and made him exceedingly great.

2Solomon spoke to all Israel, to the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, to the judges and to every leader in all Israel, the heads of the fathers' houses.

3Then Solomon and all the assembly with him went to the high place at Gibeon, for the tent of meeting of God was there, which Moses the servant of the LORD had made in the wilderness.

4But David had brought up the ark of God from Kiriath-jearim to the place David had prepared for it, for he had pitched a tent for it in Jerusalem.

5The bronze altar that Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, had made was there before the dwelling of the LORD, and Solomon and the assembly sought Him there.

6Solomon went up there to the bronze altar before the LORD, which was at the tent of meeting, and offered a thousand burnt offerings on it.

7That night God appeared to Solomon and said to him, "Ask what I shall give you."

8Solomon said to God, "You have shown great loyal love to David my father, and have made me king in his place.

9Now, LORD God, let Your word to David my father be confirmed, for You have made me king over a people as many as the dust of the earth.

10Now give me wisdom and knowledge, so that I may go out and come in before this people, for who can judge this great people of Yours?"

11God said to Solomon, "Because this was in your heart, and you have not asked for riches, wealth or honor, or the life of those who hate you, and have not even asked for long life, but have asked for wisdom and knowledge for yourself, so that you may judge My people over whom I have made you king,

12wisdom and knowledge are granted to you. I will also give you riches, wealth and honor such as none of the kings before you had, and none after you will have."

13So Solomon came from the high place at Gibeon, from before the tent of meeting, to Jerusalem, and he reigned over Israel.

Horses and Chariots

14Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen. He had one thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, and he stationed them in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.

15The king made silver and gold as common in Jerusalem as stones, and he made cedars as plentiful as the sycamore trees of the lowland.

16Solomon's horses were brought out of Egypt and from Kue; the king's traders bought them from Kue at a price.

17They brought up a chariot from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver and a horse for a hundred and fifty, and so they brought them out by their hand for all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram.

Notes

  • v3 "the high place at Gibeon, for the tent of meeting of God was there" — Kings says only that Solomon went to Gibeon for that was the great high place (1 Kings 3:4). Chronicles gives the reason a high place was lawful: the tent Moses made and its altar stood there (1 Chronicles 16:39; 21:29), while the ark was in a tent in Jerusalem (v4).

  • v5 "The bronze altar that Bezalel… had made… sought Him there" — the altar of Exodus 38:1, made by Bezalel son of Uri son of Hur (Exodus 31:2). Va-yidreshehu can be sought Him, the LORD, or sought it, the altar; the Greek has it. Seek the LORD is this book's word for faithfulness (1 Chronicles 22:19; 28:9).

  • v7 "That night God appeared to Solomon" — Kings has in a dream by night (1 Kings 3:5); Chronicles does not mention a dream.

  • vv9–10 "as many as the dust of the earth… go out and come in before this people" — the promise to Abraham, I will make your seed like the dust of the earth (Genesis 13:16), now a people to be judged. Go out and come in before them is what Moses asked for in a successor, so that the congregation of the LORD may not be like sheep that have no shepherd (Numbers 27:17).

  • v10 "wisdom and knowledge" — chokhmah u-madda. In Kings Solomon asks for a listening heart, lev shome'a (1 Kings 3:9). Madda, knowledge, is found again only in Daniel 1:4, 17 and Ecclesiastes 10:20.

  • v13 "from the high place at Gibeon" — the Hebrew has la-bamah, to the high place, which cannot stand with from before the tent of meeting… to Jerusalem. The Greek has ek, from. The text follows the Greek.

  • vv14–17 horses from Egypt — the law of the king: he shall not multiply horses for himself, nor make the people return to Egypt in order to multiply horses (Deuteronomy 17:16). Chronicles sets the horse trade right after the gift of wisdom and riches; Kings tells it at the height of his glory (1 Kings 10:26–29).

  • v15 "silver and gold as common… as stones" — Kings has silver alone (1 Kings 10:27); Chronicles adds gold.

chapters.title: Solomon and Hiram
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 2

Solomon's Letter

1Solomon gave orders to build a house for the name of the LORD and a house for his kingdom.

2Solomon counted out seventy thousand men to carry loads, eighty thousand to cut stone in the hill country, and three thousand six hundred to oversee them.

3Solomon sent to Hiram king of Tyre, saying, "As you dealt with David my father, and sent him cedars to build himself a house to live in —

4I am about to build a house for the name of the LORD my God, to dedicate it to Him, to burn fragrant incense before Him, for the bread set out continually, and for burnt offerings morning and evening, on the sabbaths, the new moons and the appointed feasts of the LORD our God, as Israel must do forever.

5The house I am building will be great, for our God is greater than all gods.

6But who is able to build Him a house, since heaven, even the highest heaven, cannot contain Him? Who am I, that I should build Him a house, except as a place to burn incense before Him?

7So now send me a man skilled to work in gold, silver, bronze and iron, and in purple, crimson and blue, who knows how to engrave, to work with the skilled men who are with me in Judah and Jerusalem, whom David my father provided.

8Send me also cedar, cypress and algum timber from Lebanon, for I know that your servants know how to cut the timber of Lebanon. My servants will be with your servants

9to prepare timber for me in abundance, for the house I am building will be great and wonderful.

10For your servants, the woodcutters who fell the trees, I will give twenty thousand cors of crushed wheat, twenty thousand cors of barley, twenty thousand baths of wine and twenty thousand baths of oil."

Hiram's Answer

11Hiram king of Tyre answered in a letter that he sent to Solomon: "Because the LORD loves His people, He has made you king over them."

12Hiram said, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who made heaven and earth, who has given King David a wise son, endowed with insight and understanding, who will build a house for the LORD and a house for his kingdom.

13Now I am sending a skilled man, endowed with understanding, Huram-abi,

14the son of a woman of the daughters of Dan, and his father was a man of Tyre. He knows how to work in gold, silver, bronze and iron, in stone and wood, in purple, blue, fine linen and crimson, and to do every kind of engraving and carry out any design that is given him, with your skilled men and the skilled men of my lord David your father.

15Now let my lord send his servants the wheat and barley, the oil and wine, of which he has spoken.

16We will cut whatever timber you need from Lebanon and bring it to you as rafts by sea to Joppa, and you will take it up to Jerusalem."

The Guests at Work

17Solomon counted all the guests who were in the land of Israel, after the census that David his father had taken of them, and they were found to be a hundred and fifty-three thousand six hundred.

18He made seventy thousand of them carry loads, eighty thousand cut stone in the hill country, and three thousand six hundred oversee the people at work.

Notes

  • v1 the numbering — in the Hebrew this verse is 1:18, and vv2–18 are 2:1–17. The text follows the English numbering.

  • v3 "As you dealt with David my father… —" — the sentence has no second half: as you did… [so do with me]. The Greek leaves it unfinished too. In Kings the letter begins differently, with why David could not build (1 Kings 5:3).

  • v3 "Hiram" — the Hebrew of Chronicles writes Churam, Huram, here and through the book; Kings writes Chiram, Hiram (1 Kings 5:1). The Greek has Cheiram in both books. He is the same king.

  • v6 "heaven, even the highest heaven, cannot contain Him" — ha-shamayim u-shemei ha-shamayim lo yekhalkeluhu, the words of Solomon's prayer at the dedication, The heavens, even the highest heavens, cannot contain You (1 Kings 8:27). Here he says it before a stone is laid.

  • v10 "crushed wheat" — chittim makkot, beaten wheat. Kings has chittim makkolet, wheat as food (1 Kings 5:11); the two words differ by one letter.

  • v11 "Because the LORD loves His people" — the reason the queen of Sheba gives: Because the LORD loved Israel forever, He has made you king (1 Kings 10:9). Here a king of Tyre says it first.

  • v12 "the God of Israel, who made heaven and earth" — in Kings Hiram says only Blessed be the LORD today (1 Kings 5:7). In Chronicles the foreign king names the LORD as maker of heaven and earth.

  • vv13–14 "Huram-abi, the son of a woman of the daughters of Dan" — le-Churam avi, Huram my father, father as a title, as Joseph was a father to Pharaoh (Genesis 45:8). Kings calls him Hiram, the son of a widow of the tribe of Naphtali (1 Kings 7:14). Of the daughters of Dan: Bezalel built the tabernacle with Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan (Exodus 31:6), and the house has a man of Dan at the work again.

  • vv17–18 "all the guests who were in the land of Israel" — ha-gerim, the men David had gathered to cut the stone (1 Chronicles 22:2). The three numbers are those of v2: the workforce is the guests.

chapters.title: The Building of the House
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 3

The Site and the Measures

1Solomon began to build the house of the LORD in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where the LORD had appeared to David his father, at the place that David had prepared, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

2He began to build in the second month, on the second day, in the fourth year of his reign.

3These are the foundations Solomon laid for building the house of God: the length, in cubits of the old standard, was sixty cubits, and the width twenty cubits.

4The porch in front, across the width of the house, was twenty cubits long, and its height was a hundred and twenty. He overlaid it inside with pure gold.

The Great House

5He paneled the great house with cypress wood, overlaid it with fine gold, and worked palm trees and chains on it.

6He adorned the house with precious stones for beauty, and the gold was gold of Parvaim.

7He overlaid the house with gold, its beams, its thresholds, its walls and its doors, and he engraved cherubim on the walls.

The Most Holy Place

8He made the room of the Most Holy Place. Its length, across the width of the house, was twenty cubits, and its width twenty cubits. He overlaid it with fine gold, six hundred talents.

9The weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold. He overlaid the upper rooms with gold.

10In the room of the Most Holy Place he made two cherubim of sculptured work, and they overlaid them with gold.

11The wings of the cherubim were twenty cubits long. One wing of the one, five cubits, touched the wall of the house, and its other wing, five cubits, touched the wing of the other cherub.

12One wing of the other cherub, five cubits, touched the wall of the house, and its other wing, five cubits, met the wing of the first cherub.

13The wings of these cherubim spread out twenty cubits. They stood on their feet, and their faces were toward the house.

14He made the veil of blue, purple, crimson and fine linen, and worked cherubim on it.

The Pillars

15In front of the house he made two pillars, thirty-five cubits high, and the capital on the top of each was five cubits.

16He made chains, in the inner sanctuary, and put them on the tops of the pillars, and he made a hundred pomegranates and put them on the chains.

17He set up the pillars in front of the nave, one on the right and one on the left. He called the one on the right Jachin and the one on the left Boaz.

Notes

  • v1 "on Mount Moriah, where the LORD had appeared to David" — the name is found elsewhere only in Genesis 22:2, the land of Moriah, where Abraham was sent to offer Isaac. There the place was named for seeing: On the mountain of the LORD it will be seen (Genesis 22:14). Here, nir'ah, He appeared, from the same verb: at Ornan's threshing floor David saw the messenger of the LORD, and the LORD answered him with fire (1 Chronicles 21:16, 26).

  • v3 "cubits of the old standard" — ba-middah ha-rishonah, by the first measure, an older standard than the writer's own. Ezekiel's measuring cubit is a cubit and a handbreadth (Ezekiel 40:5). The measures, sixty by twenty, are those of Kings (1 Kings 6:2).

  • v4 "its height was a hundred and twenty" — the house itself was thirty cubits high (1 Kings 6:2); Kings gives the porch no height (1 Kings 6:3). The Greek also has a hundred and twenty. The text keeps the number.

  • v6 "gold of Parvaim" — a place named only here. Where it was is not known.

  • v10 "cherubim of sculptured work" — ma'aseh tsa'tsu'im, a word found only here, of uncertain meaning. The Greek has a work of wood, as Kings has the cherubim made of olivewood (1 Kings 6:23).

  • v13 "their faces were toward the house" — the cherubim of the tabernacle faced one toward the other… toward the cover (Exodus 25:20). These stand on their feet and face the house.

  • v14 "the veil of blue, purple, crimson and fine linen… cherubim on it" — the veil of the tabernacle, of blue and purple and crimson and fine twisted linen… with cherubim (Exodus 26:31). Kings has doors of olivewood at the entrance of the inner sanctuary (1 Kings 6:31) and no veil.

  • v15 "two pillars, thirty-five cubits high" — Kings has eighteen cubits (1 Kings 7:15). The text keeps the Hebrew of each.

  • v16 "chains, in the inner sanctuary" — ba-devir, which does not fit pillars standing at the porch; the Greek copies the word, en tō dabeir. The text keeps the Hebrew.

  • v17 "Jachin… Boaz" — Yakhin, from kun, to establish, the verb of the promise to David, I will establish his throne forever (1 Chronicles 17:12). Boaz is the name of David's great-grandfather (Ruth 4:21).

chapters.title: The Furnishings of the House
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 4

The Altar, the Sea and the Basins

1He made an altar of bronze, twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide and ten cubits high.

2He made the sea of cast metal. It was round, ten cubits from brim to brim and five cubits high, and a line of thirty cubits measured its circumference.

3Under it, all around, were figures of oxen encircling it, ten to a cubit, going around the sea. The oxen were in two rows, cast with it when it was cast.

4It stood on twelve oxen, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south and three facing east. The sea was set on them, and all their hindquarters were toward the inside.

5Its thickness was a handbreadth, and its brim was made like the brim of a cup, like a lily blossom. It held three thousand baths.

6He made ten basins, and set five on the right and five on the left, for washing. In them they rinsed what was used for the burnt offering, and the sea was for the priests to wash in.

The Lampstands, Tables and Courts

7He made ten lampstands of gold as prescribed for them, and set them in the nave, five on the right and five on the left.

8He made ten tables and placed them in the nave, five on the right and five on the left. He made a hundred bowls of gold.

9He made the court of the priests and the great court, and doors for the court, and overlaid their doors with bronze.

10He set the sea on the right side, to the southeast.

Huram's Work

11Huram made the pots, the shovels and the bowls. So Huram finished the work that he did for King Solomon in the house of God:

12the two pillars, the bowls and the capitals on the tops of the pillars, and the two networks to cover the two bowls of the capitals on the tops of the pillars;

13the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks, two rows of pomegranates for each network, to cover the two bowls of the capitals on the pillars;

14the stands, and the basins on the stands;

15the one sea, and the twelve oxen under it;

16the pots, the shovels, the forks and all their utensils. Huram-abi made them for King Solomon for the house of the LORD, of burnished bronze.

17In the plain of the Jordan the king cast them, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zeredah.

18Solomon made all these utensils in great abundance, for the weight of the bronze could not be found out.

The Gold Furnishings

19Solomon made all the furnishings that were in the house of God: the golden altar, the tables with the bread of the Presence on them,

20the lampstands and their lamps of pure gold, to burn before the inner sanctuary as prescribed;

21the flowers, the lamps and the tongs, of gold, of the purest gold;

22the snuffers, the bowls, the dishes for incense and the fire pans, of pure gold; and the entrance of the house, its inner doors to the Most Holy Place and the doors of the house to the nave, of gold.

Notes

  • v1 "an altar of bronze, twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide and ten cubits high" — Kings names the bronze altar (1 Kings 8:64) but gives no measures. The altar of the tabernacle was five cubits long and five cubits wide… and three cubits its height (Exodus 27:1).

  • v3 "figures of oxen" — demut beqarim. Kings has peqa'im, gourds, in the same sentence (1 Kings 7:24). The two Hebrew words differ in two letters; the Greek of Chronicles has calves. The text keeps the Hebrew of each.

  • v5 "It held three thousand baths" — Kings has two thousand baths (1 Kings 7:26). The text keeps the Hebrew of each.

  • v6 "the sea was for the priests to wash in" — Kings does not give its use. Chronicles gives it the work of the bronze basin of the tabernacle, from which Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and their feet (Exodus 30:18–19).

  • vv7–8 "ten lampstands… ten tables" — the tabernacle had one lampstand and one table (Exodus 25:23, 31). Kings has ten lampstands (1 Kings 7:49); Chronicles has ten of each.

  • vv11, 16 "Huram… Huram-abi" — in v11 the name is written Chiram, Hiram, and read Churam, Huram; the text follows the read form. In v16 he is Churam aviv, Huram his father, the title of 2:13.

  • v17 "between Succoth and Zeredah" — Kings has Zarethan (1 Kings 7:46).

  • v18 "the weight of the bronze could not be found out" — lo nechqar, was not searched out, as David had said: bronze and iron beyond weighing, for there is so much of it (1 Chronicles 22:14).
